question: What is the defining architectural innovation of a modern cloud data warehouse?
options: Storing all data in row-oriented format for fast single-row lookups
The separation of storage from compute, so each scales independently over shared data
Requiring physical servers to be provisioned for peak load
Transforming data in an external engine before loading it
explanation: The core innovation is decoupling durable storage (in cloud object stores) from elastic compute clusters, enabling independent scaling, workload isolation, and paying for compute only while it runs.

question: A cloud data warehouse is optimized for which type of workload?
options: OLTP: many small, fast, single-row transactions
Real-time single-row key-value lookups
High-frequency individual record updates
OLAP: large read-heavy analytical queries and aggregations over many rows
explanation: Cloud data warehouses are OLAP systems built for large analytical queries over many rows. Using them for OLTP-style single-row operations is an anti-pattern that performs poorly and costs more.

question: Why do cloud data warehouses use columnar storage?
options: Because analytical queries read a few columns across many rows, so reading only those columns avoids loading unused data and compresses far better
Because it is ideal for updating individual rows quickly
Because it eliminates the need for any compute
Because it prevents all data duplication
explanation: Columnar storage lets the engine read only the columns a query needs (e.g., SUM(amount)) and compress similar values together (dictionary, run-length). It is a poor fit for single-row lookups/updates.

question: Which cloud data warehouse is characterized as serverless, measuring compute in slots with no clusters to manage?
options: Amazon Redshift (provisioned RA3 clusters)
Snowflake (virtual warehouses)
Google BigQuery
Teradata
explanation: BigQuery is serverless: there are no clusters to size or start, compute is measured in slots allocated automatically, and on-demand pricing bills by bytes scanned. Snowflake uses virtual warehouses; Redshift uses node clusters.

question: Dashboards are slow every morning while the nightly load runs. Which cloud-warehouse concept best fixes this?
options: Switching all tables to row-oriented storage
Disabling auto-suspend on all warehouses
Running SELECT * to warm the cache
Isolating workloads by running the load on a dedicated warehouse and BI on a separate reporting warehouse over the same shared storage
explanation: The load and reporting are sharing compute, so the load starves dashboards. Workload isolation, giving each its own compute cluster over shared storage, removes the contention.
